explanation: A constituent-closing head: at each token it attends (weight 0.4-0.95) to an earlier non-initial function word that opens the current phrase, and it writes on the token that carries that phrase's right edge. It fires (0.3-0.9 of max) on the head noun and closing qualifier of a superlative noun phrase in a declarative clause ('the tallest player [on]', 'worst storm [ever]', 'most expensive cars [in]', 'busiest street [of]', 'best'/'worst' + 'of'), and (0.3-0.6) on a mid-text fronted modifier - a subordinator ('if', 'while', 'when', 'unless', 'since', 'before', 'after', 'although', 'without') or a fronted PP ('in', 'on', 'for') - peaking on its closing comma or the main-clause subject/auxiliary that follows ('...holds, we will', '...soon, the match'); it stays below the active line (0.1-0.25 of max) on plain declarative prose, on minimum-degree 'least' phrases, on bare recipe imperatives whose only superlative sits in the object NP ('Use the deepest pan of the set for the stew'), and on the same subordinator or PP when it is the text's very first token (sentence-initial 'If/While/When/After/Although/Since/Unless/Before/As/Through/Without/Because' clauses read 0.10-0.25, because at position 0 the head self-attends and keeps writing from the text's first token), while code and math-template lines are only a weak, unreliable trigger (declaration lines such as 'class Foo', 'import java.util.List;', 'static final String NAME' clear the line at 0.3-0.6, a short isolated '#define NAME VALUE' stays at 0.18, and templated 'Let x = ...' lines reach 0.3-0.8).
